articles.title: Thomas Tuchel denies England players were distracted by Manchester City verdict
articles.summary: Tuchel says England ‘will learn’ from 3-2 loss to Spain. City’s Nico O’Reilly and Marc Guehi at fault in defeat. Thomas Tuchel denied that Manchester City being found guilty of breaching the Premier League’s financial rules is a distraction for the club’s England representatives after Nico O’Reilly…
body: News that City had been found guilty on all but one of the 115 charges against them broke on Friday afternoon, dragging the attention away from England’s preparations for their Nations League game against the world champions at Wembley a day later. It did not stop Tuchel from starting Guéhi, O’Reilly and Elliot Anderson against Spain but the topic was on the agenda after England’s first game since the World Cup ended in disappointment.

Although England met demands to play on the front foot after collapsing in their World Cup semi-final against Argentina they lived to regret Harry Kane missing a penalty when they led Spain 2-1 in the second half. But while defensive errors proved costly – Guéhi and O’Reilly gifted Spain two goals – Tuchel is confident that the storm encircling City is not an issue.

“I won’t comment on it as it’s an ongoing case,” England’s manager said. “I didn’t make it a topic. It was not a topic for me. I’m just thinking about Spain, and the team and meetings. Not for me. The players have more time than me so for sure I can imagine that they talk about it. It’s good that they do. I don’t think it was a distraction for them.”

articles.title: USA thrash Peru as teenage newcomers shine in first step toward 2030
articles.summary: Eleven players make US debuts in Orlando. Sullivan, 16, starts in youngest US appearance in years. Ellis and Hall score as Pochettino’s new faces impress. Playing in their first match of the 2030 World Cup cycle, the US men’s national team crushed Peru 4-1 in at Orlando’s Inter&Co Stadium on…
body: Sullivan received the lion’s share of the attention in the lead-up to Saturday’s match but it was Orlando City’s Ellis who stole the show early, nodding home a Gio Reyna free kick in the fourth minute to give the US an early lead. Playing in his home stadium, Ellis himself was involved in the build-up that led to the free kick, part of a nifty interchange with midfielder Malik Tillman that ended with Ellis drawing a foul at the near side of the pitch some 25 yards from goal. Reyna’s service was excellent; Ellis’ headed finish was awkward but perfectly-placed at the far post.

USMNT head coach Mauricio Pochettino’s roster for this international window features a blend of regulars alongside a host of uncapped young players, many of whom featured in Saturday’s match. All told, 11 players received their first cap for the US, with three of them – Sullivan, Ellis and New England Revolution defender Peyton Miller – in Pochettino’s starting XI. Bournemouth and 2022 World Cup captain Tyler Adams was given the captain’s armband for the first time during Pochettino’s two-year term as US head coach.

articles.title: Internationals hold three-point lead over US
articles.summary: The Internationals team could secure a first President's Cup in 28 years on Sunday after holding off a United States fightback on day three in Medinah.
body: The Internationals were behind in every match at one stage but will go into Sunday's singles holding a 10-5-7.5 lead.
The hosts had the better of the morning session, winning two and tying one of the four-balls.
But the teams split the afternoon foursomes, with Canada's Corey Conners saving par at the 18th to win the final match on the course and preserve the Internationals' three-point lead.
The International team have only won the President's Cup once since its inception in 1994 and never on American soil.

articles.title: Justin Verlander leaves field in tears with daughter after final start of 21-year career
articles.summary: Daughter Genevieve surprises 43-year-old on mound. Three-time Cy Young winner ends 21-season career. Verlander finishes with 3,560 career strikeouts. Justin Verlander got an unexpected hook in his major league finale when his 7-year-old daughter came to the mound with Detroit Tigers manager AJ…
body: After Brandon Lowe hit a foul popup starting the sixth, Hinch walked from the dugout toward the plate and pointed toward the seats. Genevieve Verlander, wearing a Tigers jersey with her dad’s name and number, sprinted to the mound and hugged her father, who reached down to embrace her and started shaking and sobbing.

Hinch joined them about 25 seconds later for another hug, and then Verlander was surrounded by Tigers teammates who came to the mound. The 43-year-old right-hander, a 10-time All-Star and three-time Cy Young Award winner over 21 major league seasons, left the field for the final time, holding his daughter’s hand, as the Comerica Park crowd gave him a standing ovation.

His wife, model Kate Upton, held 1-year-old son Bellamy while joining Justin and Genevieve for a group hug on the warning track in front of the Tigers dugout, and Justin high-fived teammates and doffed his cap to the crowd before descending the dugout steps with his family.
In all, there was a five-and-a-half-minute wait until reliever Tyler Kinley threw his first pitch.

articles.title: Laver Cup back in the balance as Team World match their captain Andre Agassi’s energy
articles.summary: Alex de Minaur recovers from match point down to beat Alexander Zverev. Carlos Alcaraz launches comeback of his own to leave event level at 5-5. For much of his afternoon on court against Alexander Zverev, Alex de Minaur seemed destined to end his day with an excruciating defeat.
body: No matter how grim the scoreline appeared, though, every effort he made was punctuated by roars of approval from one person in particular. There were loud screams of encouragement, pounding of chairs and stamping of feet. At one point, as doubt had crept into Zverev’s game during the second set tie-break, that unmistakable voice from the sidelines yelled out: “Check his oil! Check his oil!”

Those words came from Andre Agassi and, with such unconditional support provided by one of the greatest tennis players of all time, his Team World captain, there was no way that De Minaur could lose. De Minaur’s probing soon revealed that Zverev had indeed run out of oil, his engine failing, as the Australian recovered from match point down to close out a 2-6, 7-6 (5), 11-9 win.

Agassi’s unbridled enthusiasm and support was reflected in his team as they held their own on day two of the Laver Cup against a group of higher-ranked opponents. With Team Europe leading 3-1 overnight, Learner Tien of the US opened the day with a 6-3, 2-6, 10-7 win over the Italian Flavio Cobolli before De Minaur defeated Zverev, the recent French and US Open champion.

articles.title: Fisher outpoints bloodied Pirotton on Zuffa debut
articles.summary: British heavyweight Johnny Fisher wins his first fight under the Zuffa Boxing banner with a majority points victory over Michael Pirotton at the Copper Box Arena.
body: British heavyweight Johnny Fisher won his first fight under the Zuffa Boxing banner with a majority points victory over a bloodied Michael Pirotton at London's Copper Box Arena.
The 27-year-old Essex fighter was the deserved winner in a close bout, but looked laboured at times and appeared to feel the pace over 10 rounds.
Belgian Pirotton, 30, was hampered by a cut around the eye from early in the fight but battled gamely.
He was rocked in the final round as Fisher briefly threatened a stoppage, but Pirotton held on as the judges scored it 95-95, 98-92 and 96-95.

articles.title: Tuchel rues 'big mistakes' - did Man City charges have impact?
articles.summary: England's loss to Spain was decided by uncharacteristic mistakes, with two Man City players making errors - so did club news affect performances for country?
body: It was a match full of world-class players - but England's loss to Spain was ultimately decided by uncharacteristic mistakes.
Just a day after Manchester City were found guilty of breaking Premier League financial rules, two errors by City players - Nico O'Reilly and Marc Guehi - gifted world champions Spain two goals.
And former City midfielder Rodri, who moved to Barcelona in the summer, also gave away a penalty in Spain's 3-2 win on Saturday.
Pundit Roy Keane was among those left to wonder whether news of the verdict had affected players with City ties.

articles.title: How Jannik Sinner’s reign as world number one can end within the next month
articles.summary: Since recapturing world number one status by beating Carlos Alcaraz in the Monte-Carlo Masters final earlier this year, Jannik Sinner has reigned supreme atop the ATP rankings.
body: The Italian has spent a total of 24 weeks as the world number one, during which he has clinched two ATP Masters 1000 crowns, as well as a second consecutive Wimbledon title. His overall tally of weeks at number one is now 90, which ranks 10th all time.

Sinner has been largely untroubled at the top spot since Alcaraz suffered a wrist injury that kept him sidelined for four months. But now, after his US Open triumph, world number two Alexander Zverev is really applying the pressure.

Sinner currently has a points tally of 11,500, which is set to fall to 11,000 after his withdrawal from the China Open, where he is the defending champion. Zverev, on the other hand, has 9,690 ATP points to his name and has the chance to gain more in Beijing following his quarterfinal exit there last year.

Should Zverev win the China Open, only 910 ATP points will separate him and Sinner. His first chance of becoming the world number one will come at the next tournament, the Shanghai Masters, but it relies on Sinner withdrawing.

articles.title: Week 3 Fantasy Football Start 'Em, Sit 'Em: Rashod Bateman vs. Jalen Coker
articles.summary: There is a group of WRs with high ceilings going into Week 3 of fantasy football, and two of those players are WRs for the Baltimore Ravens, Rashod Bateman, and WR for the Carolina Panthers, Jalen Coker.
body: Coker through two weeks has been one of the biggest breakouts in fantasy, based on where his ADP was coming into the 2026 season. He currently has 16 receptions for 204 yards and two TDs, helping him be WR5 currently in fantasy in PPR formats. In Week 3, he and the Panthers will take on the Cleveland Browns.

The Browns have had a high and low outing regarding their passing defense's performance in two games. Against the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 1, they allowed WR Parker Washington to record five receptions for 83 yards and a TD, in a 34-10 win. He could have had a much bigger performance if the game was closer. The Jaguars only attempted five passes in the second half. Against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 2, they held their WR1, Emeka Egbuka, to three receptions for 16 yards and a TD.

Bateman stepped up in a big way for the Ravens in Week 2 with their WR1 Zay Flowers out with an injury. He recorded seven receptions on nine targets for 88 yards and a TD. For the week in fantasy in PPR formats, he was WR9. Baltimore may need a similar outing in Week 3 against the Dallas Cowboys, with Flowers' snap count uncertain.

articles.title: How GM Les Snead's philosophy has benefitted the Rams
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Rams remain Super Bowl contenders after a 1-1 start to the season because of their star-studded roster and potential. General manager Les Snead has become known for his "(Expletive) them picks" statement and philosophy over the years.
body: The philosophy led to the acquisition of veteran players such as Matthew Stafford, Jalen Ramsey and Von Miller in exchange for high draft picks. The Jacksonville Jaguars traded Ramsey to the Rams during the 2019 season, while Los Angeles acquired Stafford and Miller in 2021.
The Rams reached the Super Bowl during the 2018 and 2021 seasons, winning the latter game against the Cincinnati Bengals, 23-20, at SoFi Stadium.
Stafford remains the veteran leader for the Rams as the organization faces a familiar opportunity with the Super Bowl back in Los Angeles again this season.
Snead made two more trades, adding cornerback Trent McDuffie and edge rusher Myles Garrett during the offseason.

articles.title: Internationals take shock lead over USA into singles after late drama
articles.summary: The International Team moved another step closer to a historic Presidents Cup win on American soil by taking a 10.5-7.5 lead over Team USA into the Sunday singles.
body: Geoff Ogilvy's side held a four-point advantage after the first two days at Medinah Country Club, following their historic foursomes sessions sweep on Friday, then added 1.5 points from four matches during a tight Saturday fourballs session.
Team USA captain Brandt Snedeker benched world No 1 Scottie Scheffler for the afternoon foursomes, where they threatened their own session sweep after grabbing the early lead in all four matches.

Cameron Young and Chris Gotterup thrashed Adam Scott and Sungjae Im 6&4, before Patrick Cantlay and Xander Schauffele saw off Tom Kim and Si Woo Kim 2&1 to reduce the deficit further, only for the Internationals to fight back in an impressive finish.

Ryan Fox and Min Woo Lee bounced back from falling behind early to defeat Sam Burns and Wyndham Clark 3&2 in the bottom match, guaranteeing the Internationals would start the Sunday singles ahead for just the fourth time ever.

articles.title: Desman Stephens' hit on Dante Moore was ugly. His reaction drew even more criticism
articles.summary: LOS ANGELES — Southern California linebacker Desman Stephens II is receiving backlash for what appeared to be him celebrating following his vicious and unsportsmanlike hit that severely injured Dante Moore.
body: Early in the second quarter of Saturday's the Big Ten battle, Moore was scrambling inside USC territory when he was sliding and Stephens used his forearm to hit Moore directly in the head. Moore's head hit the grass and he wasn't moving immediately afterward as support staff and teammates rushed to check on him.

Meanwhile, Oregon players went to confront Stephens and after a small scuffle finished, Stephens was still seen celebrating the late hit as he made his way back to the sideline. While Moore was attended to in a scary moment inside Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum, Stephens was seen on the NBC broadcast smiling and high-fiving teammates. He was assessed a target penalty and disqualified from the game.

Given the nature of the hit, people across social media condemned Stephens not only for the play, but how he acted afterward while Moore was still down. Oregon coach Dan Lanning appeared to be frustrated with Stephens' reaction as he checked on his quarterback.
At halftime, most members of the NBC studio crew said Stephens' antics were "inappropriate" and a bad look for USC.

articles.title: Keane disagrees with Gordon: There is a gap between Spain and England
articles.summary: Roy Keane disagreed with Anthony Gordon's assessment that England are at the same level as Spain after the World Cup winners came from behind to beat Thomas Tuchel's side 3-2 in their Nations League opener.
body: Spain extend their unbeaten run to 39 games with the win at Wembley, but the game could have had a very different outcome had Harry Kane not missed a second-half penalty after he headed England 2-1 in front before the break.

The momentum shifted in Spain's favour after Kane's slip, with Alex Baena equalising off the bench before setting up the winner, scored by fellow substitute Mikel Oyarzabal, who broke England hearts in the Euro 2024 final.
Gordon, who scored England's equaliser from a terrific counter-attacking move, felt the performance was enough to win them the game and showed that they are a top team.

"I don't think there is a gap [to Spain] I feel like we're right there," Gordon told ITV Sport. "We can win that game so easily. If the penalty goes in we can go on and win the game. In hindsight it's always easy to say that. But I felt good in the game.

articles.title: Spain show their class as errors cost England in Nations League loss
articles.summary: Spain showed why they are the best national team in the world by emerging 3-2 winners from a thrilling, chaotic Nations League clash at Wembley, in which England's flaws undermined their exciting attacking play.
body: It was the World Cup final that might have been had England not squandered their advantage against Argentina this summer - but Spain showed the gap in quality in a result which is a major blow to Thomas Tuchel's stated aim of winning this competition.

Bad errors from Marc Guehi and Nico O'Reilly helped Lamine Yamal and Alex Baena score Spain's first two and England were cut open through the match, including for Mikel Oyarzabal's winner which came with 16 minutes to play.

Anthony Gordon had urged England to lean into their traditional strengths this week and they did just that with an exceptional counter-attack to make it 1-1, which saw the winger combine with Jude Bellingham before precisely applying the finish. Harry Kane's header from O'Reilly's cross made it 2-1 and capped an incredible transformation in the match.
In four minutes, Spain had conceded more goals than in their eight World Cup games combined.
